Class SysMLStateMachine

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.states.SysMLStateMachine
All Implemented Interfaces:
Runnable
Direct Known Subclasses:
ParametricAnalysisStateMachine
public abstract class SysMLStateMachine extends SysMLAnything implements Runnable
SysMLinJava's representation of the SysML state machine.

State machine for synch/asynch part behavior

SysMLStateMachine is the base class for an executable model of a finite state transition system. As such, it implements the Runnable interface and is typically executed asynchronously in its own thread of execution in the thread-pool of the context part for which it exists. However, it can be executed synchronously with the thread that submits events. The SysMLStateMachine can be defined and executed either within the context of a SysMLPart or as a "stand-alone" state machine to model/simulate a behavior.

Property of the SysMLPart

As an abstract class the SysMLStateMachine must be extended/specialized. If the specialized class for the state machine executes in the context of a SysMLPart, i.e. it is the part's state machine, then it should be instantiated/initialized within the body of the context SysMLPart's createStateMachine() operation. When used as any other behavior model, it can be instantiated within the context in which it will execute.

Near complete support for SysML/UML standard state machine

The current version of the SysMLStateMachine supports most of the standard features of the SysMLv2 "state" as well as the SysMLv1/UML state machine. This version supports basic states and transitions where states can execute actions for the OnEnter, Do, and OnExit actions of a state. Composite states and sub-state machines are supported. Pseudo states for initial, choice, and junction pseudo-states are also supported. Transitions can be specified for both internal and external transitions and can be associated with class-based triggers, guards, and effects. And event prioritization is supported. Support for history states is not yet available and is planned for a future version of the SysMLStateMachine. In any case, all but the most complex of state machines can be precisely modeled and simulated by this version of the SysMLStateMachine.

State machine execution implementation

The SysMLStateMachine includes fields for the initial and final states of the state machine. Extending classes create additional states and transitions to construct a complete state machine. This base class provides an onInitialEvent and an onEvent operation to execute the state machine. These operations receive all events that are submitted to the state machine and process them in accordance with the state machine definition. The state machine execution can be performed synchronously (same thread as caller) or asychronously (its own thread). Asynchronous exections are performed by the state machine's Runnable interface implelmenation. The implementation is, of course, the run() operation, which retrieves the events and invokes onInitialEvent and an onEvent operations that processes the events in accordance with the states and transitions specified by the extending class. This run(), onInitialEvent, and onEvent operations implement the state machine in accordance with the UML standard and should not be overridden in extending classes.

Asynchronous event handling

Asynchronous events are submitted to the SysMLStateMachine via a queueEvent(SysMLEvent) operation. Events are queued to a standard thread-safe Java PriorityBlockingQueue, thereby enabling multiple threads to submit events to the state machine. Events are queued in accordance with SysML/UML standard event prioritization. The standard SysMLPart provides an operation to submit events to the state machine indirectly via the part, but events can be submitted directly to the state machine in a thread-safe manner directly via the queueEvent() operation. Events are not prioritized in this base class for the SysMLStateMachine, but event priorities can be achieved by setting the eventComparator field with the desired comparator. If present, the eventComparator will be used to keep the events in the queue sorted accordingly.

Built in timer support

The SysMLStateMachine provides support for automatic generation of time events. Calls to the startTimer() operation create timer objects that submit TimerEvents to the state machine. Processing of the time event may invoke specified SysMLEffect-based "event handlers" that in-turn invoke transitions and their corresponding effects.

Creating the state machine

The SysMLStateMachine provides a series of overrideable method calls to create all the states, transitions, guards, and effects of the complete state machine. The SysMLStateMachine constructor automatically invokes methods to create the elements of the state machine so that extensions to the SysMLStateMachine need only override the createXxxx() operations for the applicable elements (fields) declared in the extending class to ensure the system of states and transitions is created/initialized in the correct and complete sequence needed.

Utility capabilities for parametric analysis and displays

Finally, the SysMLStateMachine base class provides capabilities to perform utility functions during the performance of transitions between and within states. The SysMLStateMachine field variable transitionsUtility of interface type TransitionsUtility is invoked whenever a state transition is performed. Transition information such as current state, triggering event, guard, effect, and next state, are passed to the utility's operations. Implementations of this interface can enable capture of the data for state transitions tables, timing diagrams, or for simple capture and storage of the transitions data for later review and analysis. In any case, capture and display of this transitions data can enable detailed analysis of the model execution and make for some audience pleasing and convincing graphics for design reviews and other presentations of the model.

See the implementation referenced below for an example of using this capability to transmit state transition table and timing diagram information to respective displays. SysMLinJava contains two rudimentary console-based applications that can receive and display the state transition table and timing diagram data as simple text. However, there are commercially available applications that provide real-time graphical displays of the tables and diagrams. These applications also provide capabilites to save/export the transition tables and timing diagrams as PDF, CSV, and HTML files enabling post-model execution review and analysis of the state transitions and timings of any or all of the state machines in the SysMLinJava model. Visit SysMLinJava.com for more information.

  • Field Details

    • initialState

      @InitialState public SysMLInitialState initialState
      The initial state of the state machine. This is a SysMLinJava defined state that is used as the starting point of the state machine behavior. Extending classes should define one transition that starts at this initial state to ensure correct initialization of the state machine. The InitialTransition class is provided as convenient option for this purpose.
      See Also:
      • SysMLInitialState
      • InitialTransition

    • finalState

      @FinalState public SysMLFinalState finalState
      The final state of the state machine. This is a SysMLinJava defined state that is used as the stopping point of the state machine behavior. Extending classes should define at least one transition that ends at this final state to ensure correct completion of the state machine. The FinalTransition class is provided as a convenient option for this purpose.
      See Also:
      • SysMLFinalState
      • FinalTransition

    • context

      public Optional<? extends StateBehaviorContext> context

The context is the parent of the state machine, i.e. the part, port, or item that executes in accordance with this state machine and whose attributes, parts, ports, or itemss may be accessed and whose actions may be invoked by the states and transitions of the state machine.

    • eventQueue

      private Optional<PriorityBlockingQueue<SysMLEvent>> eventQueue
      The optional event queue for the state machine. If set, events to the state machine are submitted to the state machine asynchronously via this queue. As a thread-safe queue, the eventQueue enables event submission by multiple execution threads, i.e. the dequeing and response of the state machine is performed in a seperate thread of execution from the threads that enque the event. If not set, events to the state machine are submitted synchronously via call to the onEvent() operation and the response of the state machine to the event is performed in the same thread of execution.

      Note:As an instance of the PriorityBlockingQueue events are priorized in the queue in accordance with the SysML/UML standard state machine event queue, i.e. completion and time events are posted to the head of the queue amongst other types of events. The default implementation of the Comparator<?> interface used for the SysMLStateMachine uses this priority logic, but SysMLinJava users may set their own value for the comparator to enable another priority scheme if needed.

    • eventComparator

      public Comparator<SysMLEvent> eventComparator
      The comparator of events submitted to the eventQueue. This comparator priorizes events in the queue in accordance with the SysML/UML standard state machine event queue, i.e. completion and time events are posted to the head of the queue amongst other types of events. SysMLinJava users may set their own value for the eventComparator to enable another priority scheme if needed. The different value of the eventComparator can be set anytime after the SysMLStateMachine class's constructor is invoked and before the first call to the start() operation.

    • count

      int count
      Runnable operation that executes the state machine asychronously (in a different thread) from the submitter(s) of events. The run() operation takes events off the event queue and processes them in accordance with the states and transitions defined by the SysMLStateMachine-based class heirarchy specified for the state machine. It invokes the onInitialEvent() operation to start the state machine (transition out of the initial state) and the onEvent() operation for all subsequent events it receives. These operations are performed in the runnable's thread of execution to perform the event processing asynchronously from other parts' state machines.

      Note this method is provided to enable model execution. It is not part of the SysML standard, To the extent the SysML standard does not provide elements for executable modeling per se, SysMLinJava includes various model elements to enable model execution.

  • Constructor Details

    • SysMLStateMachine

      public SysMLStateMachine(Optional<? extends StateBehaviorContext> context, boolean isAsynchronous, String name)
      Constructor of the state machine. The constructor sets the context part, sets the asynchronicity, and optionally sets a unique name for the state machine. It also initializes the eventQueue, the initial and final states, and invokes the creation operations that create all the elements of the state machine model.

      As an abstract class, this SysMLStateMachine's constructor must be invoked by the constructor of the class that extends/specializes the SysMLStateMachine. In turn, if the extension/specialized class is to execute within the context of a specified SysMLPart context, the constructor of the extension/specialized class should be invoked by the context's createStateMachine() operation.

      Parameters:
      context - the SysMLPart in whose context this state machine is to execute
      isAsynchronous - whether this state machine is to run asynchronously, i.e. in its own thread of execution which is different from the thread(s) that may submit/enque events
      name - name of the state machine

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start()
      Starts the state machine. That is, submits an initial event to transition out of the InitialState in accordance with the InitialTransition specified in an extending class.

      Note this method is provided to enable model execution. It is not part of the SysML standard, To the extent the SysML standard does not provide elements for executable modeling per se, SysMLinJava includes various model elements to enable model execution.

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Stops the previously started state machine. Note that this operation is a "hard" stop, i.e. if the state machine's run() operation has not ended, regardless of the state of the state machine the thread in which the state machine executes is simply cancelled (terminated).

      Note this method is provided to enable model execution. It is not part of the SysML standard, To the extent the SysML standard does not provide elements for executable modeling per se, SysMLinJava includes various model elements to enable model execution.

    • startTimer

      Parameters:
      event - the SysMLTimeEvent to be submitted to this state machine's event queue upon the specified time occurance(s). The timer's initial delay and subsequent period are specified in this event.

    • onInitialEvent

      public void onInitialEvent(InitialEvent initialEvent)
      Event handler for the initial event. That is, for the first event received by the state machine to transition from the initial state. The operation performs the initial transition then it determines the next transition, if any, that is active and performs that transition, until no active transitions are found or the final state is reached.

      Note this method is provided to enable model execution. It is not part of the SysML standard, To the extent the SysML standard does not provide elements for executable modeling per se, SysMLinJava includes various model elements to enable model execution.

      Parameters:
      initialEvent - initial event received while in initial state.

    • onEvent

      public void onEvent(SysMLEvent event)
      Event handler for the state machine. The event handler traverses the statemachine's states and transitions network in accordance with the SysML/UML standard state machine.

      This operation should not be called directly by client parts, such as SysMLFullPorts or SysMLParts. Instead submission of SysMLEvents to this operation should be done via the queueEvent() operation. (SysMLPart has an acceptEvent() operation that calls its state machine's queueEvent() operation for you}) This queueEvent() operation will correctly invoke the onEvent() operation in accordance with the synchronous nature of the state machine, i.e. if the isAsynchronous argument of the constructor was set to true, then the event will be submitted to the state machine via the thread-safe event queue, but if the isAsynchronous argument of the constructor was set to false, then the event will be submitted via a direct call to the onEvent() operation. The OnEvent operation use the following logic:
      if the current state has sub-state machines for which one or more of the these will react to the current event, then the event is enqueued to each of the sub-state machines.
      Other wise, the event is processed for the current state as follows.

      If the event is not a completion event or is a completion event and indicates all sub-state machines are completed, then the current state is queried for the next transition.
      If a next transition is found, then the next transition is performed and a new (next) state vertex is set.
      If the next vertex is not the same as the current vertex, i.e. the transition was not an internal transition, then the next vertex is set as the current vertex and the process is repeated, i.e. the next transition is found and performed.
      The process repeats until no next-transition is found.

      Note this method is provided to enable model execution. It is not part of the SysML standard, To the extent the SysML standard does not provide elements for executable modeling per se, SysMLinJava includes various model elements to enable model execution.

      Parameters:
      event - The next event to be processed in accordance with this state machine's specifed states and transitions.
      See Also:
      • queueEvent(SysMLEvent)

    • listOfStates

      public List<String> listOfStates()
      Overridable operation that should return a list of identity strings for each of the states in the state machine. This method must be overridden if the state machine's state transition times transmissions is enabled, i.e. the list is used by the enableStateTransitionTimesTransmission() operation. Specializations of the SysMLStateMachine should override this operation by invoking this base class operation and then adding its additionally specified states, and the finalState, to the list returned by this operation.

      Note this method is provided to enable model execution. It is not part of the SysML standard, To the extent the SysML standard does not provide elements for executable modeling per se, SysMLinJava includes various model elements to enable model execution.

      Returns:
      list of state names (identity strings) for states in the state machine. For this base class, the list contains only the identity string for the initialState.

    • createEventComparator

      protected void createEventComparator()
      Overridable operation that creates the event comparator that implements the Comparator<SysMLEvent> interface used by the event queue to prioritize events in the SysMLStateMachine's event queue. This operation sets the eventComparator to a default comparator which gives all events equal priority, i.e. no prioritization of events. This operation can/should be overridden in extended classes if/when event prioritization is needed.

    • createStateCompositeStateMachines

      protected void createStateCompositeStateMachines()
      Overridable operation that should create the state machines of any composite states of the state machine. The SysMLState requires all sub-state machines to be specified as a list, in which case each of the statements in this overridden operation should be the assignment of a list of state machines to this state machine's field variable for the list, similar to the following.

      An example follows: 

      
	my1stNormalOpsStateMachine = new NormalStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my1stSubSystem, "my1stNormalStateMachine", 1L);
	my2ndNormalOpsStateMachine = new NormalStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my2ndSubSystem, "my2ndNormalStateMachine", 2L);
	my3rdNormalOpsStateMachine = new NormalStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my3rdSubSystem, "my3rdNormalStateMachine", 3L);
	my4thNormalOpsStateMachine = new NormalStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my4thSubSystem, "my4thNormalStateMachine", 4L);
	my1stEmergencyOpsStateMachine = new EmergencyStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my1stSubSystem, "my1stEmergencyStateMachine", 1L);
	my2ndEmergencyOpsStateMachine = new EmergencyStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my2ndSubSystem, "my2ndEmergencyStateMachine", 2L);
	my3rdEmergencyOpsStateMachine = new EmergencyStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my3rdSubSystem, "my3rdEmergencyStateMachine", 3L);
	my4thEmergencyOpsStateMachine = new EmergencyStateMachine(((ControlSystem)context.get()).my4thSubSystem, "my4thEmergencyStateMachine", 4L);
etc.

    • createStateDoActionFunctions

      protected void createStateDoActionFunctions()
      Overridable operation that should create the action functions, if any, performed by the states' Do operation of the SysMLState.

      An example follows: 

      

	&#64;DoActionFunction
	SysMLDoActionFunction myFirstDoActionFunction;
	&#64;DoActionFunction
	SysMLDoActionFunction myNextDorActionFunction;
		:
	&#64;Override
	protected void createStateDoActionFunctions()
	{
		myFirstDoActionFunction = (context) ->
		{
			&lt;block statements&gt;
		};
		myNextDoActionFunction = (context) ->
		{
			&lt;block statements&gt;
		};
	}
      Note: the SysMLDoActionFunction is executed in its own thread, different from the one that executes the state machine. The Do action thread is started immediately after completion of the SysMLOnEnterFunction and is either terminated (canceled) if/when a transition-causing event is received by the state machine, or self-terminates after run-to-completion. In the latter case, the the Do action should perform a queueEvent() of a SysMLCompletionEvent to the state machine to enable state transitions that depend on such completions, if any.
      See Also:
      • SysMLDoActionFunction

    • createStates

      protected void createStates()
      Overridable operation that should create the state machine's states.

      An example follows: 

      protected void createStates()
{
        super.createStates();
        myFirstState = new SysMLState(context, "FirstState");
        mySecondState = new SysMLState(context, Optional.of(secondOnEnterAction), Optional.of(secondDoAction), Optional.of(secondOnExitAction), "Second");
        myThirdState = new SysMLState(context, Optional.of(thirdOnEnterAction), Optional.empty(), Optional.empty(), "Third");
        myEmergencyState = new SysMLState(context, Optional.empty(),
        List.of(my1stEmergencyOpsStateMachine, my2ndEmergencyOpsStateMachine, my3rdEmergencyOpsStateMachine, my4thEmergencyOpsStateMachine), Optional.empty(), "EmergencyOps");
        myOtherState = new SysMLState(context, "Other");
}
      where the first statement is invoking the states creation of the superclass, i.e. a default creation of the FinalState. Other statements create the states of the state machine as object creation expressions. The target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the State annotation. The value of the assignment is one of the new SysMLState() constructors for the state.

      Note: All states must be declared as type SysMLState. The current version of SysMLinJava does not recognize extension classes for the state. Also, the InitialState and FinalState should not be created in this operation. These states are created by the overridden operation, which must be invoked as the first statement in this operation.

      See Also:
      • SysMLState

    • createPseudoStates

      protected void createPseudoStates()
      Overridable operation that should create the state machine's pseudo-states.

      An example follows: 

      
super.createPseudoStates();
myJunctionPseudo = new SysMLJunctionPseudoState(context, "MyJunction");
myChoicePseudoState = new SysMLChoicePseudoState(context, "MyChoice");

      Note: All pseudo-states must be declared/initialized as type SysMLInitialState(), SysMLJunctionPseudoState(), or SysMLChoicePseudoState(). The current version of SysMLinJava does not recognize extension classes for these pseudo-states. Also, other pseudo-states are not yet implemented in SysMLinJava.

      See Also:
      • SysMLInitialState
      • SysMLJunctionPseudoState
      • SysMLChoicePseudoState

    • createGuardConditions

      protected void createGuardConditions()
      Overridable operation that should create the conditions that define the transition guards.

      Code format: 

      
myFirstGuardCondition = (event, context) ->
{
	part statement;
};
mySecondGuardCondition = (event, context) ->
{
	part statement;
};

      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the GuardCondition annotation and the assignment expression is a lambda expression with parameters event and context that represent the SysMLEvent that triggered the transition and the part in whose context the state machine is executing, respectively. The lambda expression is an implementation of the SysMLGuardCondition functional interface.

 myFirstGuard = new SysMLGuard(myFirstGuardCondition, "FirstGuard");

      protected void createEffects()
      Overridable operation that should create the state machine's effects, if any, that are used as effects of transitions.

      Code format:

      
myFirstEffect = new SysMLEffect(context, myFirstEffectAction, "FirstTransitionEffect");
myNextEffect = new SysMLEffect(context, myNextEffectAction, "NextTransitionEffect");
etc.

      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the Effect annotation and SysMLEffect() is the constructor for the effect.

      • SysMLEffect

    • createTransitions

      protected abstract void createTransitions()
      Overridable abstract operation that should create the state machine's transitions that are used as transitions between and within states. The transitions created must include the initial transition needed for the state-machine to start execution, i.e. the InitialTransition. Use of the FinalTransition to transition to the FinalState is optional, but the state machine will continue to execute unless and until it reaches the FinalState, so if the FinalTransition is not used, a correctly constructed SysMLTransition must be used to transition to the final state.

      The InitialTransition must indicate a previous state of the InitialState type and the FinalTransition (or a SysMLTransition to the final state) must indicate a next state of the FinalState type. The SysMLStateMachine declares and constructs an instance of the InitialState named initialState and of the FinalState named finalState that can/should be used for this purpose.

      Typically, the InitialTransition will be initialized (constructor call) as the first statement in this createTransitions() operation. The new InitialTransition constructor's nextState will be a state specified in the specialization of the SysMLStateMachine and the FinalTransition will be initialized (constructor call) with a prevState as an arbitrary state specified in the specialization of the SysMLStateMachine. All other transitions can be initialized with desired prevState/nextState combinations as well as with specified triggers, guards, effects, and kinds.

      Transitions from a state should have triggers and guards that result in only zero or one transition being available for execution by the state machine. Typically, this means all trigger/guard pairs for transition within or out of a state should be unique. If more than one transition is available for execution, the transition that is selected is undefined. However, the current implementation of the state machine will select the first transition declared in this createTransitions() operation that is available for execution, i.e. the first constructed transition that has the correct trigger and a satisfied guard or a null guard.

      Example code format:

      
    intialTransition = new InitialTransition(context, initialState,  firstState, "Initial";
   myFirstTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,   firstState, secondState, Optional.of(FirstTriggerEvent.class), Optional.of(firstGuard), Optional.of(firstEffect), "First", SysMLTransitionKind.external);
  mySecondTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,  secondState,  thirdState, Optional.empty(), Optional.of(secondGuard), Optional.empty(), "Second", SysMLTransitionKind.external);
myInternalTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,  secondState, secondState, Optional.of(SecondTriggerEvent), Optional.of(secondGuard), Optional.of(secondEffect), "Internal", SysMLTransitionKind.internal);
   myFinalTransition = new SysMLTransition(context,   thirdState,  finalState, Optional.of(ThirdTriggerEvent.class), Optional.of(thirdGuard), Optional.empty(), "Final", SysMLTransitionKind.external);
--OR--
   myFinalTransition = new FinalTransition(context,   thirdState,  finalState, "Final");
etc.

      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the Transition annotation and new InitialTransition(), new SysMLTransition(), and new FinalTransition() is the constructor for the transition.

      Note: All transitions (except the InitialTransition and FinalTransition) must be declared as type SysMLTransition. The current version of SysMLinJava does not recognize specialized/extension classes for the transition.

      See Also:
      • SysMLTransition
      • InitialTransition
      • FinalTransition

    • createRequirements

      protected void createRequirements()
      Overridable operation that initializes the state machine's requirements. An example follows: 
      @Requirement
public SysMLRequirement myFirstRequirement;

@Requirement
public SysMLRequirement myNextRequirement;

      myFirstRequirement = MySysMLRequirements.firstSysMLRequirement;
myNextRequirement = MySysMLRequirements.nextSysMLRequirement;
      where the the target of the assignment operation is the name of a field with the &#64;Requirement annotation and MySysMLRequirements.firstSysMLRequirement is a reference to an instance of a SysMLRequirement in an extension/specialization of the SysMLRequirements class.

      Note that state machine requirements should be declared as described above, i.e. as references to instantiations of SysMLRequirements declared and initialized in classes that extend/specialize the SysMLRequirements class. Requirements should not be declared/initialized in the state machine itself. Requirement specifications in the typical SysML model are collected in a model package where they can be easily queried and managed. The SysMLinJava approach of collecting requirements in a single class emulates this method.

      See Also:
      • SysMLRequirementsCollection

    • createDependencies

      protected void createDependencies()
      Overridable operation that creates the dependencies for this state machine. Overrides of this operation should perform initializations of variables annotated as dependencies. Whereas dependencies are types of association, each dependency should be defined by a field annotated as a 
      @Dependency
public APartBlock aPartDependency;
      and initialized by an object reference For example: 
      aPartDependency = ((ParentBlock) context).bPartBlock;
      where aDependency is the name of a variable that represents a dependency (trace, usage, etc} of this part on another model element. Note the assignment value should be a reference to another model element, and not to a "new" object (constructor).
